title: Fort Collins group plans 'No Kings Day' protest in response to D.C. military parade - NewsBreak
text: As thundering tanks and thousands of soldiers fill the streets of central D.C. for a military parade June 14 , Fort Collins organizers are planning to take part in a nationwide protest of the event. Indivisible NoCo will gather for "No Kings Day" — a nationwide protest meant to "demonstrate against monarchy" — from 10 a.m. to noon June 14 at Colorado State University. The protest will take place south of the university's Lory Student Center, according to a news release from the group. The D.C. military parade is planned in celebration of the U.S. Army's 250th anniversary. It will feature tanks, artillery, flyovers by vintage warplanes and soldiers in historic uniforms dating back to the American Revolution. It caps off a week of programming "designed to celebrate the country's military might," according to reporting by USA TODAY. The June 14 parade also coincides with Flag Day and President Donald Trump's 79th birthday. "For two and a half centuries the men and women of America's army have dominated our enemies and protected our freedom at home. This parade salutes our soldiers' remarkable strength and unbeatable spirit," Trump said in a video message posted to his Truth Social account June 5. The procession will begin at 4:30 p.m. MT and will be livestreamed on all U.S. Army social media platforms. The Army estimates the parade will cost around $40 million, which includes the cost of repairing streets expected to be damaged by the parade's tanks, according to USA TODAY. Are fireworks legal in Fort Collins? A new city ordinance makes citations easier "No Kings Day" protests were planned across the country as counterprogramming to the parade June 14 . They follow similar "Hands Off!" and "May Day" demonstrations organized against Trump and billionaire Elon Musk, who led the administration's polarizing Department of Government Efficiency before his late-May departure from the White House. Indivisible NoCo organizers reject the military parade, calling it an "extravagant and costly" military celebration that comes at a time when "budget cuts threaten essential programs like Social Security, SNAP, Medicaid and Medicare," the group's news release reads. Flag Day, the group contents, is to celebrate the U.S. flag's history and the principles it represents — freedom, justice, unity, patriotism. "Now, more than ever, we must come together to ensure the principles of democracy endure for another 250 years," the release reads. USA TODAY reporters Kathryn Palmer, Joey Garrison and Tom Vanden Brook contributed to this report. For more from reporter Erin Udell, subscribe to The Buzz, her weekly newsletter about Northern Colorado business, development, real estate and restaurants. This article originally appeared on Fort Collins Coloradoan: Fort Collins group plans 'No Kings Day' protest in response to D.C. military parade
